newsitem.title: USA: US Diagnostic fails Nasdaq listing test.
newsitem.headline: US Diagnostic fails Nasdaq listing test.

text.p: US Diagnostic Inc said Tuesday it has been informed by Nasdaq it does not "satisfy the net tangible asset test" for continued listing on the National Market Systems.

In a quarterly filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission, the Florida-based company said it had been informed by the electronic stock market on May 13 following review of its annual report for year ended December 31, 1996.
This does not mean the stock will be delisted, a spokeswoman for Nasdaq said. The company has the option for being listed as a smallcap stock. However, none of this takes place immediately.

The company has requested a review of the staff determination, saying it is in solid financial condition and its net tangible asset deficit is the result of an acquisition that benefited the company and its shareholders.

The company said Nasdaq has recognized the need to accommodate companies that are unable to satisfy the net tangible asset test because of large amounts of goodwill associated with merger and acquisition activities.
US Diagnostic said it will request such an accommodation.
